instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `ffi_integer_return`. extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0. On x86-64 System V ABI: - Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX. It should compile and run successfully.
description: extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0. On x86-64 System V ABI: - Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX.
comments: extern "C" integer returns must use RAX, not XMM0.
On x86-64 System V ABI:
- Integer-returning C functions (i32/i64/bool) return in RAX.
- Float-returning C functions (f64) return in XMM0.
Sounio's internal convention carries all values (including f64) as
bit-patterns in RAX.  When we call an extern "C" fn that returns
an integer, RAX is already correct — no fixup is needed.
The bug was that strip_extern_blocks() discarded extern "C"
declarations entirely, causing callers to receive xor-eax-eax (0)
via the undefined-variable fallback, so pid was always 0.
The fix: strip_extern_blocks() now parses each extern "C" fn decl
and emits a Sounio stub that calls the correct platform mechanism
(syscall for integer-returning OS functions; native impl for math).
The stub returns its result in RAX — the Sounio calling convention —
so the return-register dispatch is always correct.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gradient_descent_from_compiler`. sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio. β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the. It should compile and run successfully.
description: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio. β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
comments: sensitivity_of() implemented via β⁴ shadow buffer in lean_single.sio
THE SURPRISE: gradient descent in Sounio.
β⁴'s per-channel sensitivity buffer stores ∂y/∂x_k — literally, the
gradient of y with respect to each uncertain input x_k, computed by
the compiler at emit-time via forward-mode automatic differentiation.
We expose this via the new `sensitivity_of(y, k)` builtin. That turns
Sounio — a language originally designed for epistemic typed computing —
into an automatic-differentiation language.
To prove it: minimize L(x) = (x − 3)² by gradient descent, using the
compiler's sensitivity as the gradient. No external library. No manual
derivative. The compiler knows dL/dx because it computed it while
emitting the code.
Starting x = 0. Learning rate 0.1. 30 iterations.
Expected: x → 3.0, L → 0.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_interprocedural_topology`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural). Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/ multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural). Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/ multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-3 regression (inter-procedural).
Week-2 tracked channel topology through let-bindings, additive/
multiplicative ops, and two-arg builtins (atan2, pow).  It did NOT
union topology across user-defined function calls — the return
inherited only the *last* argument's channel set.
Concretely, for
fn my_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a + b }
let x = k0.value   // channel 0
let y = k1.value   // channel 1
hessian_of(my_sum(x, y), 0, 1)
week-2 left EXPR_CH_SET = {ch1} (only y's topology), and the query
H_{0,1} was REFUSED at type-check because channel 0 was not in the set.
Week-3 unions the channel sets of every argument into the return
topology (conservative upper bound, matching the atan2/pow discipline).
The same program now type-checks.  The runtime value is 0.0 because
inter-procedural SSHADOW propagation is not yet wired — topology
tracking and shadow tracking are orthogonal concerns.  This test
asserts that the type checker accepts the query; the shadow pipeline
is covered by epistemic_hessian_*.
Single-arg fns (my_square below) were correct by accident pre-fix and
continue to work — union of one set is itself.

comments: β⁹ GTT — KAS-1 pattern is now the compiler-verified natural API.
Under Gradient Topology Types, channels are assigned at `.value`
extraction time.  Doing arithmetic on the extracted scalars yields
an expression whose topology is the union of its operands' channels.
`hessian_of(z, j, k)` is accepted iff both j, k are in z's topology.
Before GTT (Phase 4): KAS-1 was a user-assertion with a policy-level
Lean proof.
After GTT (Phase β⁹): KAS-1 IS the type discipline; violations are
rejected at type-check time (see tests/compile-fail/gtt_hessian_out_of_topology.sio).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `rapamycin_epistemic_pbpk`. Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues). It should compile and run successfully.
description: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
comments: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) Epistemic PBPK Test Suite
Validates GUM-based uncertainty propagation through a 3-compartment
rapamycin model: Blood, Brain (BBB-limited), Peripheral (fast-eq. tissues).
Model choice: Distribution-capped 3-compartment (NOT full 14-compartment).
- Brain compartment: kp_brain=0.08 (P-gp efflux at BBB) — PRESERVED accurately
- Peripheral: v_periph=50L, kp_periph=0.5 → t1/2 ~ 21h (tractable for 48h)
- Adipose deep sequestration (kp_adipose~15) excluded by design
(would require multi-week simulation for CL to be observable in AUC)
Epistemic parameters:
- cl_hepatic: 12.4 L/h, Var=54.76 (CV=60%, CYP3A4 polymorphism, Ferron 1997)
- kp_brain: 0.08, Var=0.000625 (SD=0.025, P-gp efflux, Lampen 1998)
- fu_plasma: 0.08, Var=0.0004 (SD=0.02, 92% bound, Schreiber 1991)
GUM step sizes: h = max(1e-6 * |mean|, 1e-2 * SD)  [GPT review correction]
Confidence: evidence-quality score [0,1], NOT Beta distribution
(Beta appropriate only for [0,1]-bounded quantities; CL is unbounded)
6 tests:
1. Simulation completes successfully
2. Brain/plasma ratio < 0.15 (P-gp efflux verified)
3. CV(AUC_0_48) > 30% (CYP3A4 inter-individual variability)
4. All epistemic variances > 0
5. AUC(CL/2) > AUC(CL_ref) — causal monotonicity check
6. CL dominates AUC uncertainty: s_cl > 0.5

description: - Tests for the differential geometry module Self-contained test suite for metric tensors, Christoffel symbols, Riemann curvature, Gaussian curvature, geodesic integration,
comments: test_diffgeo.sio -- Tests for the differential geometry module
Self-contained test suite for metric tensors, Christoffel symbols,
Riemann curvature, Gaussian curvature, geodesic integration,
parallel transport, and index raising/lowering. All helpers and
functions copied from stdlib/math/diffgeo.sio.
Tests:
1.  Euclidean metric is identity: diag(1,1,1)
2.  Metric inverse of identity: g^{-1} = g for Euclidean
3.  Flat space Christoffel symbols = 0
4.  Flat space Riemann tensor = 0
5.  Sphere 2D Gaussian curvature = 1 (unit sphere)
6.  Sphere metric at equator: g = diag(1, 1)
7.  Schwarzschild metric at r=10: g_tt ~ -0.8, g_rr ~ 1.25
8.  Geodesic in flat space is straight line
9.  Parallel transport preserves norm in Euclidean space
10.  Hyperbolic plane curvature = -1
11.  Metric determinant of sphere: det(g) = sin^2(theta) at theta=pi/4
12.  Raise and lower index roundtrip

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `gtt_reassignment_wrong_channel`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology). After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x] with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:. It should fail to compile.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology). After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x] with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology).
After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x]
with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
var r = k0.value     // r: {ch0}
r = k1.value         // r: {ch1}  (ch0 is gone)
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)  // REFUSED: channel 0 not in {ch1}
This matches the semantics of let-binding — the variable's topology
reflects its *current* value's topology, not its history.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `tac_compile_gate_refuse`. Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path. `prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: EpistemicComplete violation.
description: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path. `prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
comments: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path.
`prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry
compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
`measure(8.0, uncertainty: 4.0)` yields confidence = 1 − 4.0/8.0 = 0.5
= 500/1000, BELOW the 800 threshold. The compiler is required to
REJECT this program — no binary is emitted, the rejection is enforced
before any runtime check would run. Diagnostic from
lean_single.sio:20984-21006 prints
`error: EpistemicComplete violation in fn main ... (conf=500 < 800)`.
Clinical narrative: pre-TDM (n=0 samples), the only available C24h
estimate is the wide popPK prior with CV ≥ 50%. The compile-time
rejection prevents code that would prescribe under insufficient
evidence — a guarantee runtime gates cannot give.
